What does it really take to create a life by design instead of simply managing one by default? 
A Ritz Thing is about creativity and becoming — not just your best self, but who you were created to be.
Through candid conversations and honest solo episodes, we explore creativity, entrepreneurship, relationships, personal growth and everything in between. Expect different perspectives, practical insights, laughter and some uncomfortable truths. The good, the bad and the beautifully messy. 
If you're ready to move with intention and purpose, join the conversation and subscribe to A Ritz Thing.

title: Shave.net
author: Shave.net
description: Wet shaving, minus the mystique and the razor burn. Safety razors and which blade to load, straight razors for the brave, building a proper lather from soap or cream, shaving with the grain and against it, and the small habits that separate a clean shave from a neck full of bumps. Each episode takes one part of the routine — prep, lather, passes, aftercare, kit care — and works through it practically, with a bit of humour and no gatekeeping. Written for anyone who shaves and suspects they could be doing it better, from first-time safety razor buyers to people with a drawer full of soaps. Five or six minutes, one topic. Topics include choosing a safety razor and blades, straight razors and shavettes, brushes and lathering, pre-shave prep, shaving direction and passes, razor burn and ingrown hairs, sensitive skin, aftershave and beard care, and keeping your kit clean. Produced by Shave.net, wet shaving gear and advice. Full details, products and further reading at https://shave.net

title: More Than an Athlete | Faith, Identity, Athlete
author: Callie Levin | Division 1 Basketball Player
description:
Do you ever feel like your whole day revolves around your sport? Practice, workouts, extra reps, film, recovery, yet somehow you still don’t feel like you’re doing enough? More Than an Athlete is the weekly podcast for athletes who love their sport but lately feel like it has become their whole world.
 Hosted by Callie Levin, a Division I basketball player at the University of Northern Iowa, we talk about everything from the pressure to perform to dealing with failure, comparison, and figuring out who you are outside of your sport. 
Through my own stories and experiences, I’ll connect the realities of being an athlete to faith, identity, and what it looks like to find more joy in your sport. Whether you’re a high school or college athlete trying to navigate the highs and lows of your sport, this podcast is a place to feel understood, encouraged, and reminded that you are so much more than what you do.

title: Psychology of a Serial Killer | True Crime, Forensic Psychology, Criminal Profiles
author: Jonah White & Jaxon Foss | Criminology and Mental Health Major
description: Have you ever wondered if the warning signs of a serial killer were there all along? Are you looking for true crime content that doesn’t just retell the story, but also dives into the psychology behind it? Psychology of a Serial Killer is the weekly podcast that dives deep into the minds of killers and the reasons behind their behavior. Hosted by Jaxon Foss and Jonah White, we explore factors such as childhood trauma, abuse, personality disorders, fantasies, obsessions, and their need for power and control. Whether you’re a true crime enthusiast or just a casual listener, this podcast is here to show you what TRULY goes on in their twisted minds. As hosts with backgrounds in both criminology and mental health, we have spent our education researching exactly what this show explores. Each episode is researched thoroughly in order to provide the most accurate representation of case history and psychological state. Through digging into the case files behind these crimes, we discovered that understanding a killer’s psychology isn’t about excusing what they’ve done. Instead, it is about learning to recognize and identify the warning signs before they escalate. Now, we want to share with you the specific disorders that can be connected to specific killers, episode by episode. If you’re looking to actually understand what the warning signs of serious psychological issues look like, Psychology of a Serial Killer is where you’ll find extensive research that is grounded in real psychology and paired with a serial murder case. Join us as we dive into the mind of John Wayne Gacy and his struggle with Antisocial Personality Disorder, David Berkowitz and Schizophrenia, Jeffrey Dahmer and Borderline Personality Disorder, and many more. So, if you’re ready to understand the mind of a murderer, tune into Psychology of a Serial Killer, available wherever you get your podcasts. Don’t miss an episode of the true crime podcast that treats the psychology as seriously as the story.

Life Is Meant to Be Lived is a storytelling podcast highlighting people with physical disabilities who choose to live fully despite adversity. Through honest, emotional, and hope-filled conversations, host Molly Harper shares stories of resilience, faith, purpose, and what it means to keep showing up for life when it looks different than expected.
While these stories center on physical disability, this podcast is for anyone navigating hardship and needing a reminder that even in difficult seasons, life still holds meaning, beauty, and possibility.

Welcome to AI Transformation & Governance, the podcast that makes complex AI topics easy to understand, helping leaders and professionals unlock AI potential while keeping risks under control.

title: From The Boys
author: Michael McGlone
description:
What is it to be a boy in London in 2026?

There is a lot of talk in the media about the problem of boys, but the conversation too often doesn’t include us or reflect our experiences. In this podcast we set the agenda and talk about the things that really matter to us, to share our experiences from our own perspectives.


We are year 10 boys from William Ellis School in north London. For our podcast series From the Boys, we have set out to voice our perspectives in this changing world of societal pressures and expectations on boys. We are aware there are many discussions around boyhood, however we want to involve boys of our age in these discussions to truly show how we feel and what we experience. In each episode, we talk to a range of people from educational specialists, teachers, young men and boys with different and important viewpoints.


This podcast is for boys and those who are interested in their experiences.

We hope that this podcast spreads awareness of the issues boys are actually facing.

We hope that this podcast breaks the stereotypes of boys.

We hope that this podcast raises awareness of some of the issues boys face and some of the misconceptions about them.

We hope this podcast gives boys a chance to have their voices heard.

From the Boys is an MDX Studios Production, copyright 2026.


This podcast was created by Ahmed, Kente, Daniel, Jacob, Bobby, Patrick, Isaaq, Oskar, Muhamed, Tyrese, Ethan, Guillem, Kobi, Rabah, Arda and Félix from William Ellis School, in the London Borough of Camden.

It's a chance to go beyond the familiar names and faces and get to know these extraordinary individuals in a whole new way.

Their stories. Their insights. Our community.

title: Beneath the Surface with Matt and Troy
author: Lighthouse Church
description: Beneath the Surface with Matt & Troy is more than just a conversation about Sunday's sermon. It's an opportunity to dig deeper into God's Word, unpack biblical truths, and explore how the Gospel applies to everyday life. Each episode, Matt and Pastor Troy take a closer look at Sunday's message while tackling real-life questions, faith, culture, and the challenges of following Christ in today's world. Our goal is simple: to move beyond surface-level faith, grow in our understanding of Scripture, and keep the Gospel at the center of every conversation.

title: Beyond Burnout with Leslie Glen
author: leslieannglenbeyondburnout
description:
Beyond Burnout explores psychology, mindfulness, and what it means to live well in a world that never seems to slow down. Therapist Leslie Glen looks at burnout, the pressures that shape us, and the ways we can reconnect with our feelings, needs, values, and capacity.
Through thoughtful conversations and practical reflections, this podcast invites you to move beyond simply coping—and start asking what kind of life you actually want to live. Leslie has a master’s degree in psychology and training in CBT and EMDR.

title: IsMOMok?
author: Cherished Mom
description:
Is MOM ok? makes space for honest conversations about maternal mental health—the struggles we keep quiet, the support we need, and the stories that remind us we’re not alone.
Through personal stories and conversations with advocates and experts, we explore postpartum psychosis, loss, and the many emotional realities of motherhood. We’re breaking the silence, challenging stigma, and bringing awareness and prevention of maternal suicide into the conversation.
Whether you’re a mom, love a mom, or support moms in your work, you belong here. Because asking “Is MOM ok?” is only the beginning.

title: Lost in Germany Podcast
author: Bruna & Cynthia
description:
Two women. Two countries. One confusing new life in Germany.
We're Bruna and Cynthia. Brazilian and French. We met in a German class because we were lost in the same way. 
Lost in Germany is our monthly podcast about building a life here from scratch: the paperwork, the loneliness, learning German as adults, and the small wins. No sugar-coating. No expat guide nonsense. Just honest conversations.

title: Synergy 7 2026! Session 1, Friday Evening
author: Synergy Sessions
description:
One Spirit. Seven Expressions.

Launching into Season 3, this episode is the Friday evening session of the Synergy: Seven Gathering, that took place in Dunfermline, Scotland 18-19th September, 2026. A partnership of Streams Creative House and Cairn Movement and then many other friends.


Charity Bowman-Webb and Robyn Stewart of Streams Creative House kicked off Synergy: Seven with this session teaching, preaching, and modelling healthy prophetic giftings in the Church of our Lord Jesus. 


At the heart of this gathering is a simple but urgent question: what does it mean to respond faithfully and courageously in this time? As familiar models are being reshaped, Synergy 7 creates space to explore how the Church can rediscover its missionary edge through the full expression of fivefold leadership—apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers working together to equip God’s people.


The future of the Church will be discovered by seeking God’s heart and rediscovering the fullness of His Spirit. 

Discover with us.

title: Sunshine Circle Podcast

description:

Hosted by Marcia Michelle Reeves, the screenwriter and producer behind the film, each episode is an honest, heart-first conversation about overcoming childhood trauma and finding the strength to move forward.

Marcia sits down with guests who aren’t afraid to get real about what shaped them, what they carried into adulthood, and how they began to heal. No sugarcoating, no shortcuts, just real stories and real hope.

If you’ve ever wondered whether healing is possible, pull up a seat. You’re already part of the circle. ☀️

description:
The world gives us plenty to talk about. I want to know what we’re going to do with it.
I’m Precious “Preciosa” Myers-Brown, your Chief Innovation and Dream Officer™, and this is The Unhinged Voice™ with PMB. This is where I pull up to the desk and talk through what’s happening in the world and what it means for us living our best life. Work, money, AI, faith, health, culture, relationships, reinvention. If it touches how we live, it belongs in the conversation.
For decades, I’ve challenged the personal, professional, cultural, institutional and technological constructs that limit what people, organizations and systems believe is possible. At 50, my entire world shifted. After everything I had built, everything I had poured myself into, it became very real to me how much of my life could be affected by somebody else’s decisions. I decided I would never again put myself in a position where I needed permission to be who I am, or where someone else got to decide what I could do with my talents.
I’m unhinging from those arrangements and building a life where I have more say over my time, my work, my money and my possibilities. That’s the conversation I’m bringing to this desk, and I want us to have it together. Let’s question what we’ve accepted, explore what’s possible and put it to use as we build toward the Four Freedoms: financial, location, flexibility and fun.
Every episode is day one. Whatever you’ve been waiting to start, change or claim, whenever you find this, today can be your day one.

I’m Dr. Sue, a sexologist, health educator, and author who spends a lot of time talking about things we don’t always talk about. 
Because honestly? Sex ed was never the end of the story. For a lot of us, it was barely the beginning. 
Our bodies, relationships, health, pleasure, and all the messy stuff that comes with being human are more complicated than anything we learned in health class. And so often, we have questions we never learned how to ask.
I’ll be joined by experts, other voices, or sometimes it’ll just be me, going deeper into the questions that make being human so interesting.

title: Blessing birthday
author: jarikhan
description:
Welcome to Birthday Blessings & Wishes! 🎂 Discover heartfelt birthday blessings, beautiful birthday wishes, meaningful prayers, and inspiring messages for friends, family, and loved ones.

Whether you are looking for a special birthday blessing, a heartfelt prayer, or the perfect words to make someone's birthday memorable, you'll find inspiration here.


Celebrate every birthday with love, happiness, gratitude, and positivity!

title: Anarchists of the Ordinary
author: The Numbersmiths
description:
A New Era for Numbers. This is a business and astrology podcast exploring the alchemisation of money, creativity, psychology and human behaviour. Hosted by Melissa, founder of The Numbersmiths, we bring Western psychological astrology down to Earth, unravelling subconscious patterns and the collective undercurrents shaping our world. We deconstruct outdated business models, honour our natural seasons and cycles, and explore what it means to create a business and a life that financially supports the human living it. A space to unfurl, ripen and become something beyond the ordinary. Less beige. More pleasure. More practical. More play.

Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.

title: Singula Talks
author: Anton
description: Singula Talks is conversations with the people running businesses — CTOs, CEOs and founders. Not about the companies, but about the people behind them: how they think, how they decide, and what got them there. Careers and turning points, building and running teams, AI and the way work is changing, and where the industry goes next. New episodes on Spotify, Apple Podcasts and YouTube. Hosted by Anton.

title: Life with the Roberts
author: Jared and Alyssa Roberts
description: Life with the Roberts is all about real life, real stories, and lessons learned along the way. We're a married couple talking about the ups, the downs, the unexpected moments, and everything in between. Our hope is to encourage you, make you laugh, and remind you that we're all figuring this thing called life out together.

title: Scarlett and the Treasure Map

description: An interstellar pirate adventure, featuring catchy and beautiful songs for children.

title: Crime Scene Vienna
author: Arienne Bettstetter and Moritz Grün
description:
Crime Scene Vienna is a True Crime podcast where we explore real criminal cases in Vienna, Austria.

author: Ayrshire Healing Centre
description:
Welcome to Beyond Ordinary Reality, from Ayrshire Healing Centre.
A space for curious minds, open hearts and conversations that don’t always fit neatly into boxes. Join us for Conscious Conversations exploring spirituality, holistic healing, energy, life, death and all things weird and wonderful — alongside guided meditations, sound baths and immersive healing experiences.
Some episodes will make you think. Some will help you switch off. Some might take you somewhere completely unexpected.
Come curious. Leave a little more connected.

title: EVERYDAY INTEGRITY
author: Dawn and Margie
description: Everyday Integrity is a podcast dedicated to exploring how integrity shapes our lives—both in ordinary moments and pivotal decisions. Our mission is to inspire honest reflection, authentic living, and conscious choice-making through real stories and practical insights. By turning awareness into action, it encourages each of us to live with greater truth, purpose, and alignment every day.

title: Invest Like the Best with Patrick O'Shaughnessy
author: Horror

the WELLNESS APPROACH is where science meets real-life wellness. Hosted by the experts at Timeless RX & Primal RX we dive into hormones, weight loss, aesthetics, peptides, and all things wellness—breaking down complex topics into honest, easy-to-understand conversations.
Whether you’re looking to feel better, look better, or simply understand your body more deeply, this podcast is your seat at the table for education, empowerment, and lasting health.

title: On Time Collectors Series | Presented By 0260 and The Miami Watch Club
author: Lex Borrero
description: On Time Collector Series is a conversation-driven show exploring watch collecting beyond hype and price. We sit down with collectors, designers, and industry leaders to talk about taste, legacy, personal milestones, and the emotional reasons people collect. Real stories, real wrists, timeless perspective.

title: Everyday People with Euan
author: 96three FM
description: Euan is one of the friendly voices you’ll hear on 96three through each weekday - sharing faith, encouragement and the very best in Christian music. Beyond the microphone, Euan is a qualified psychotherapist who works with students and young adults in schools, supporting their wellbeing and mental health. With a faith-filled curiosity and a genuine heart for people, Euan loves exploring the stories of everyday people, the challenges they’ve faced, the triumphs they’ve celebrated, and the moments God has met them along the way. Because every life has a story worth hearing, and at the heart of every story is a God who loves us relentlessly.

author: Tiffany Gilliam
description: A daily ten-minute reset for your mind. Evidence-based self-development, mindset shifts, and one small practice a day, brought to you by Tiffany Gilliam, author of Mindset Mastery: Harnessing the Power Within for Success and Fulfillment.

title: Minds Of Freedom - 3 Minutes of Praise
author: Minds Of Freedom
description:
Three minutes. One intentional pause. A powerful shift.
MOF: 3 Minutes of Praise is your invitation to step away from the noise and spend three intentional minutes focusing on God instead of everything competing for your attention.
Through scripture, gratitude, encouragement, and praise, each episode is designed to help you reset your thoughts, strengthen your spirit, and remember that your circumstances do not get the final word.
Whether you’re starting your morning, sitting in your car, taking a break, or need a spiritual reset any time, day or night, take three minutes and turn your attention toward the One who can change everything.
You’ve given the problem enough of your time. Give God three minutes of your praise.
Minds of Freedom — Gratitude shifts attitudes. True Freedom Begins In The Mind.

title: Personal in passing
author: Bahi
description: Bahi approaches a stranger, sits down, and asks real questions. What emerges is never what you'd expect: a story, a perspective, a moment of connection. title: Leading Under Fire: Tough Conversations for Managers
author: John Faisandier
description:
There is a conversation you have been putting off. Maybe it is with someone on your team who keeps missing the mark. Maybe it is with your own boss. You think about it in the car. You think about it on Sunday night.

Leading Under Fire is for team leaders and managers who handle difficult conversations, tension and conflict at work, and who want to do it without losing sleep or losing the relationship.

Your host is John Faisandier. He has spent more than 25 years helping people stay calm and clear when things heat up. He has worked with frontline staff, team leaders and CEOs across New Zealand and Australia, including teams at Fonterra, Datacom and Greater Wellington. He is the author of the book Thriving Under Fire: Turn Difficult Customers into Business Success.

Some episodes are short and give you one useful idea. Others go deeper, with the stories and background behind how John helps managers through the hard moments. You will hear about managers who got it wrong, and managers who got it right. Every episode gives you something you can use.

You will learn how to:

•       Stay calm when someone gets stuck into you

•       Hold people to account without damaging the relationship

•       Give honest feedback without triggering defensiveness

•       Stop carrying work conflict home with you

•       Say no in a kind way and mean it

Conflict isn't the enemy. Avoidance is. Struggling with hard conversations is not a character flaw. It's a training gap, and it's fixable.

Find out more at tuf.co.nz

title: Arctos x Teddy Sin - Coffee Break, Market Take
author: Teddy Sin
description: Every trading morning, in the time it takes to drink a coffee, Teddy walks through yesterday's markets: US indices, the Nikkei, gold, oil and Malaysia. What moved, and which way the pressure leans. Market education, not financial advice.

title: Figuring It Out With Vicki
author: Vicki
description:
Figuring It Out with Vicki exists because none of us ever truly have life figured out.
I’m a woman in my forties who has discovered that the more I learn, the more I realize there is still so much I don’t know. That realization isn’t discouraging—it’s exciting. It has taught me that growth doesn’t come from having all the answers. It comes from asking better questions.
This podcast is built on curiosity.
It’s for people who believe learning shouldn’t stop. It’s for people who wake up wanting to become a little wiser, healthier, kinder, and more prepared than they were yesterday.

title: Still Figuring it Out
author: Lily
description:
Still Figuring it Out is a podcast about life, love, growing up, and everything in between. I’m your host, Lily, this is a space for honest conversations about the things we’re all trying to navigate- relationships, friendships, confidence, career, change, and the moments when you have absolutely no idea what you’re doing next. 
Because the truth is, nobody really has it all figured out.

title: Hitmaker Radio CHR
author: Hidden Producer Studios
description: Hitmaker Radio CHR brings together listener created songs and Hitmaker Originals, where singer-songwriters work through unfinished lyrics and creative choke points to end with a Hitmaker Hit! New Music never heard before across both CHR Hit Music and Hit Country Music with deep dives into the creative process and the final outcomes.

title: The Briefing Room
author: Michelle Hess, Jason Shaffer
description: The Briefing Room is for leaders who are tired of the noise and ready to lead with clarity. Hosted by Michelle R. Hess and Jason Q. Shaffer, each conversation digs into the real questions behind leadership, including how to gain clarity, build trust, and create impact that lasts. Guests span public service, business, faith, and beyond. They're leaders shaping their industries and communities, wherever they're leading from.

title: The Music City Tribune
author: The Music City Tribune News Desk
description: Welcome to The Music City Tribune Podcast — Nashville's home for outrageous headlines, Southern humor, and hilarious fictional news!From Broadway's honky-tonks to Nashville's neighborhoods, we poke fun at Music City's quirks, tourists, traffic, and everyday absurdities.The Music City Tribune — Where Nashville Gets Ridiculous!Visit TheMusicCityTribune.com for more.All stories are fictional satire created for entertainment.

title: SHARE Journeys
author: SHARE
description:
For years, Lizzy Savetsky has been one of the loudest voices fighting for the Jewish people. But somewhere along the way, she lost her why.
In Lizzy’s Journey, she goes back to the source. Each week she sits down with one of Judaism’s leading rabbis and teachers to ask the questions she couldn’t answer on her own. Why are we here? What does it really mean to be Jewish? What does Kabbala teach about the soul? And how do you keep going when the fight gets heavy?
With Rabbi Benji Levy, Rabbi Manis Friedman, Rabbi Shlomo Farhi, Rabbanit Shani Taragin, Rabbi Simon Jacobson, Fally Klein and Rabbi

title: Grim’s Weekly Reckoning
author: ECF Studios
description:
News. Narratives. Nonsense

A weekly ECF Studios podcast.


The week’s news is dead. Grim is here to examine the body.

From ECF Studios, the creators of The Evident Conspiracy Files and Grim Stories, comes Grim’s Weekly Reckoning—a darkly comic breakdown of the headlines, hidden narratives and conspiracy theories shaping the conversation.

Each week, Grim turns the page on the stories dominating the news, digs through what may have overlooked and asks the uncomfortable questions others would rather leave buried.


Expect suspicious headlines, alternative explanations, viral theories, inconvenient facts and Grim’s distinctly unforgiving sense of humour. 

Listeners are invited to submit their own views, questions and theories—and the most intriguing may be summoned into the next episode.

Some stories are serious. Some theories are absurd. Most deserve a closer look.


News. Narratives. Nonsense.
Question everything—from the shadows.

One nail tech. One art therapist. Everybody’s got something to get off their chest.
Join Bree and Laurel for File & Shrink, where your stories, secrets, and “am I wrong?” moments get two different perspectives. From relationship drama and family tension to friendships, boundaries, and the things you’re afraid to say out loud, they’ll talk it through with humor, honesty, and a few uncomfortable questions.

author: Jalisa Phoenix-Roberts
description:
What if becoming your best self isn't about changing who you are, but discovering who you truly are?
Welcome to The Secret Podcast: The Magic of Your True Authentic Self with Jalisa Phoenix-Roberts.
Join me for honest conversations about self-help, personal growth, life, identity and what it means to live authentically. We'll explore the stories we carry, question the messages we hear and discover what happens when we begin to understand, accept and trust who we really are.
Come as you are. Listen, reflect and discover more of you.

title: Your Unstuck Era: Career Change, Side Hustles & Entrepreneurship
author: Your Unstuck Era
description: Your Unstuck Era is an operator podcast about how businesses get built before the success story is obvious. Host Vivian Ly interviews early-stage founders, including the person sitting next to you at the office who is quietly building an entire company, to unpack the decisions, experiments, economics, and tradeoffs behind the build. No celebrity origin stories or billion-dollar hindsight. Just useful conversations with people close enough to the beginning to tell you how it actually works.

description:
Ancient texts. Modern events. And some remarkable connections between the two.
The Timeline is an ongoing investigation into biblical prophecy, geopolitics, artificial intelligence, and the changing systems shaping our world.
We examine original sources, challenge familiar assumptions, and follow the evidence wherever it leads—without predictions disguised as certainty.
You don't have to believe the Bible to follow the investigation. Just bring your curiosity.
The pieces are on the table. The timeline is still unfolding.

title: Manny's Mota-Vation

Big ambitions. Female hormones. And absolutely no interest in making health another full-time job.
Welcome to Locked In & Synced Up, hosted by women's health coach Elin Påfs.

title: Can’t Stop Listening

Well, today, we’re going to talk about something interesting: music addiction! Get comfortable, turn up the volume, and let’s find out why we just can’t stop listening!

Welcome to The Health Review! 🎙️

Our brand new weekly podcast is here. Each week Daniel Kirkham asks the layman's questions about the health stories making headlines: what's really going on, should we be worried, and what can we do about it naturally?

On each episode one he will be joined by Dr Sarah Myhill, a GP since 1981 who now works as a naturopathic physician, to dig into the health news and stories of that week.


Dr Myhill shares her personal views, so take what resonates and always speak to your own doctor before changing your diet or treatment.

Watch the full episode on Youtube

Through personal storytelling, Tiger Tracks invites listeners into discussions about Tower School’s exciting, academically challenging curriculum for students ages 3–14, that balances:

title: Enticed to Good
author: Camille
description:
What if those quiet, fleeting nudges in your day aren’t random at all, but God using you to answer someone else’s prayer?

On Enticed to Good, host Camille explores the quiet impressions, promptings, and inspirations that shape our lives. Through uplifting, real-life interviews, guests share their personal stories of stepping out in faith to follow a nudge—and the incredible ways God works through ordinary people to bless others.

If you’ve ever wondered how to recognize inspiration, struggled with talking yourself out of a good deed, or simply need a weekly dose of hope and joy, pull up a chair. Let’s learn to trust our first promptings and be enticed to good together.

title: CIO Confidential
author: CIO Confidential

Follow Penelope, a curious and imaginative little girl, and Dad as everyday moments turn into playful adventures filled with creativity, problem-solving, big feelings, silly surprises, and a little bit of magic. Perfect for bedtime, car rides, quiet time, or anytime you want to slow down and share a story together.

title: Can We Talk
author: AndreBaxter
description:
Life is full of questions, challenges, and situations that don't always come with easy answers. But what does the Word of God have to say about the issues we face every day?
Welcome to Can We Talk?, a faith-based podcast hosted by Apostle Dawn Skipworth, where biblical truth meets real-life conversations.
From relationships, marriage, and family to faith, personal struggles, spiritual growth, and today's toughest social issues, no topic is too difficult to discuss. Each episode takes listeners on a journey through Scripture, breaking down God's Word in a way that's practical, relatable, and applicable to everyday life.
This isn't just another Bible study. It's an opportunity to ask the hard questions, challenge misconceptions, gain spiritual understanding, and discover how God's timeless wisdom speaks to today's world.
Whether you're new to the faith, growing in your relationship with God, or simply searching for answers, there's a seat at the table for you.

title: Better.
author: Daria R G
description: This podcast is dedicated to anyone who has ever wished from the depths of their soul to get better. As a teen who had severe mental health issues for years, “better” will always be a part of how I describe myself. Being mentally better used to be all I ever wanted. I used to believe better wasn’t possible for me, but looking back, I couldn’t have been more wrong. I’m here, after years of work, not scared of my own mind anymore, (and of life) and my purpose is for you to be able feel the same. Because your mental health doesn’t define you, nor should it control you. Cheers to better.

title: The Whiteboard Updates

title: Breaking the Silence – Men's Mental Health Podcast
author: Tyrone Clinton  Uyumwunigbebe
description: Welcome to Breaking the Silence, a men’s mental health awareness podcast hosted by Tyrone Clinton Uyumwunigbebe, Mr Africa UK 2026.  This is a safe and welcoming space for honest conversations about men’s mental health, emotional wellbeing, societal expectations, relationships, fatherhood and personal growth.  Through real-life experiences, engaging discussions and conversations with guests and mental health professionals, we challenge the stigma surrounding men’s emotions and encourage open dialogue.  Our mission is simple: to remind every man that being strong doesn’t mean suffering in silence.  Because every voice matters, and every man deserves to be heard.

title: Off Book Files
author: Off Book Files

Off Book Files tells the story of the world's biggest corporate frauds through an auditor's eye. title: Each Word a Universe: Turning Bones, Not Stones
author: The Ephesus School
description:
The Greeks said each person is a universe, and built their cities so that everything would turn around man. Scripture says everything turns around God, and God is not set before us as an idea to contemplate or an image to behold, but as a scroll to be heard. Each word of that scroll carries the functionality of his scriptural universe.

Each day this podcast takes a single passage and follows one word through the three scrolls of Abraham: the Hebrew root, its Greek carrier in the Septuagint and the New Testament, and its Arabic cognate in the Qurʾan. The aim isn't to find a meaning to admire but to hear a function at work, the same consonantal skeleton speaking in Genesis, in Luke, and in the clear Arabic tongue.

This is samāʿ, hearing as turning. The prophet turns the bones of the word, as Ezekiel spoke over the valley until the dry bones came together and lived. Ours is to hear, not to pile up the stones of Babel.

A few minutes a day. One word. God at the center, and the scroll in our hands.

title: The Oldest Answer’s Podcast
author: TheOldestAnswer
description:
Long before self-help, a warrior on a battlefield in India, an emperor writing notes to himself on campaign, and a philosopher in an Athenian marketplace were asking the questions you carry around at 3 AM. How do I stop gripping what I can’t control? Who am I underneath all this noise? What does it actually mean to be free?

Worlds apart, they arrived at strikingly similar answers.

The Oldest Answer puts the Bhagavad Gita and the Upanishads in conversation with Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, Epictetus, Socrates, and Heraclitus. It’s for overthinkers and anxious modern minds who want something older and steadier than the next hot take.

It’s also a show about what happens to wisdom when it crosses an ocean. Host Raj Shankar, author of the novel Kem Cho?, came to America from India at eight. Some episodes turn toward the questions immigrant families rarely say out loud: what our parents carried with them, what didn’t fit in the suitcase, and how to find your own way into a faith that arrived smaller than it left.

Short daily episodes and a weekly deep dive. Philosophy as an invitation, never a sermon.

The Gita ends with Krishna telling Arjuna to reflect on everything he has heard, then do as he wishes. That’s the spirit here.

The opening question is the hook. It’s often all a browsing listener sees before tapping “more,” so I’d leave it first even if you rearrange the rest.

title: Making the Most of Parent-Teacher Confer
author: Anusha
description: Episode 6: Making the Most of Parent-Teacher ConferencesWelcome back to County Schools Calendar, your trusted guide to school dates, academic schedules, and important education updates across the United States!A successful school year involves more than attending classes and completing assignments. Communication between parents and teachers also plays an important role in helping students learn, grow, and reach their academic goals.In today’s episode, we’ll explore how families can prepare for parent-teacher conferences, ask useful questions, and stay involved in their children’s education throughout the 2026–2027 school year.Let’s start with understanding what parent-teacher conferences are.These meetings give parents and teachers an opportunity to discuss a student’s academic progress, classroom participation, strengths, and areas where additional support may be helpful. They also allow families to better understand classroom expectations and upcoming academic goals.So, how can parents prepare?First, check your school calendar for conference dates. Schools may schedule meetings during specific weeks, professional development days, or designated conference periods. Since schedules differ between districts, always confirm the date and time with your child’s school.Next, prepare a few questions before the meeting. You might ask how your child is progressing in different subjects, which skills they should focus on, or how you can support learning at home. Writing down your questions beforehand can help you make the most of the available time.It’s also helpful to review recent assignments, report cards, and teacher feedback. These materials can give you a clearer picture of your child’s progress and help you identify topics worth discussing.Remember, parent-teacher conferences are a two-way conversation. Teachers can share classroom observations, while parents can explain any learning challenges or concerns they have noticed at home. Working together can help create a more supportive learning environment.After the meeting, take a few minutes to review the key points. If you and the teacher agree on specific goals, write them down and check progress over time. Small, consistent steps can make a meaningful difference.Families should also stay connected throughout the year rather than waiting for formal conferences. School newsletters, parent portals, emails, and official announcements can help parents remain informed about assignments, school events, and academic updates.And this is where County Schools Calendar can help!Our website makes it easier to explore school calendars by state and county, identify important academic dates, and access links to official school district resources. Checking your school calendar regularly can help you prepare for conferences and other important events.Remember, supporting a student’s education is a partnership between families and schools. Staying informed, asking questions, and maintaining open communication can help students feel encouraged and supported.Thank you for listening to Episode 6 of County Schools Calendar!Visit our website to explore school calendars and plan ahead for the important moments in your child’s academic journey.Until next time, stay involved, stay informed, and keep making every school year count!

title: Ocean Waves ASMR Podcast

description:
Ocean Waves ASMR Podcast brings you soothing ocean sounds and gentle beach waves for deep sleep, relaxation, study and focus. Every episode is a calm, steady soundscape of small waves lapping onto soft sand, with no talking, no music and no sudden sounds. Just press play, close your eyes and let the tide carry you away.


Each episode takes you to a dream beach somewhere in the world. One night you are drifting off on a quiet white sand beach in the Maldives, the next you are studying beside the turquoise lagoon of Bora Bora, reading in a hidden cove on the Amalfi Coast or unwinding after work on Grace Bay in Turks and Caicos. From the Seychelles, Bali, Fiji and Mauritius to the Caribbean, Thailand and the Greek islands, every episode is inspired by one of the most beautiful beaches on earth, so you can picture yourself there while you listen.


The sound itself stays the same calm signature you can rely on every day: soft, rolling waves that wash gently up the shore and slide back again in a slow, even rhythm. There are no big crashing waves, no seagulls, no voices and no music. That steady, predictable sound is exactly what makes ocean waves one of the most popular relaxing sounds in the world, and a natural form of white noise that helps mask traffic, neighbours, snoring and other background noise.


USE IT FOR SLEEP

Ocean sounds for sleep are the heart of this show. Play an episode at bedtime to fall asleep faster, drift back to sleep after waking up at night or calm a racing mind. Light sleepers use the waves to cover background noise, and many listeners simply let an episode play all night.


USE IT FOR BABIES AND KIDS

Gentle ocean white noise is a favourite for baby sleep, naptime and calming a fussy or crying baby. Play it softly on a speaker across the room as part of your bedtime routine.


USE IT FOR STUDY, FOCUS AND WORK

Beach ambience makes a calm, distraction-free background for studying, exam prep, reading, writing and deep work. Working from home? Let a tropical shoreline replace the noise of your house and help you stay in a focused flow.


USE IT TO RELAX

Breathe along with the tide for meditation, yoga, mindfulness, stress relief and calming anxious moments. The waves are also perfect for a spa day at home, a massage, a long bath, a Sunday reset or simply a ten-minute mental beach holiday in the middle of a busy day.


NEW EPISODES EVERY DAY

A new episode comes out every day, each with its own destination and purpose: deep sleep in the Maldives, a power nap on Koh Lipe, focus in Bali, baby sleep in Bora Bora and many more. Look out for special episodes for Halloween, Christmas, New Year and Blue Monday, plus milestone specials along the way.


ABOUT THE CREATOR

Ocean Waves ASMR Podcast is created by ASMR creator Robin Verrue, who also makes relaxing ambient podcasts such as Relaxing Raindrops, Coffeehouse ASMR and Hair Salon Sounds ASMR. Each soundscape is carefully layered and smoothed for long, comfortable listening on headphones or speakers.


Follow Ocean Waves ASMR Podcast on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music and YouTube Music so you never miss a new beach. If the waves help you relax, please leave a rating or review. It helps other people find the show. Have a dream beach you would love to hear in a future episode? Send it to Robin.

title: ELITE VOICE: The Academic Podcast on Singing
author: ELITE VOICE
description:
There is an instrument every human being owns from birth. It sits in the throat, two folds of muscle and mucous membrane about the length of a thumbnail, and it can do far more than most people ever ask of it. Few ever learn to play it, and of those who try, many eventually give up, assuming they lack something that others were given.

This podcast is about that instrument and about how it is learned. It explains how a tone is formed, where it becomes loud, why the voice cracks on the way up, and why no one ever hears their own voice the way others hear it. It shows what happens in the breath, the heartbeat, and the blood when a person sings, and why every culture on earth has placed singing at the heart of its rituals. Above all, it pursues a question that precedes every exercise and is almost never asked in singing lessons: how a person acquires a skill whose execution they can only perceive, in themselves, in distorted form.

The answers come from research: from voice physiology, acoustics, anthropology, and above all from a hundred and forty years of learning psychology, whose findings have transformed the training of doctors and pilots while leaving voice training, vocal coaching, and singing lessons largely untouched. Every episode rests on studies that can be looked up, with place, year, and source, on questions such as why Monday’s singing lesson has all but vanished by Thursday, why the recording belongs at the start of practice rather than the end, why a single image achieves more than three instructions, and what a person who listens is worth.

This podcast is for people who want to learn to sing, for those who have tried before and want to understand why it did not work, and for teachers who want to measure their methods against what the research knows.

The conversations behind the headlines. Straight from Abu Dhabi.

What does it really take to build something that matters? Kawthar Bin Sulayem sits down with the founders, artists, doctors and community builders of the UAE and the Arab world and asks what most interviews never reach: what it took, what it cost, and what they know now.

Three ways in:

Inside Arts & Culture: the artists, curators and gallerists shaping how the region’s creative scene is seen and valued.

Start anywhere. Hear how a gallery put African art on a global stage. Meet the artist who rebuilt a vanished 1980s Palestinian wedding. Listen to a family doctor explain how to break the cycle of emotional pain.

Watch, Listen.

title: Thrive Solo
author: Lucy Meggeson
description:
Let’s be real — being single and child-free? It’s pretty damn awesome. Don’t believe me? Stick around. I promise you, by listening to this podcast, you’re going to start seeing your solo life in a whole new light — one that feels empowering, exciting, and full of possibility.

I’m Lucy Meggeson, and I’m here to help you stop seeing singlehood as a consolation prize and start embracing it as the incredible opportunity that it is. Because the truth? Being single isn’t second best. It’s not a waiting room. And it sure as hell isn’t a life of lack. In fact, when you lean into it, it can be just as fulfilling—if not more so—than being coupled up with kids.

And besides, no matter what our relationship status, what we all really want is to feel good in the here and now. So instead of focusing on what’s ‘missing,’ let’s focus on what’s possible. The freedom. The adventure. The extra time and headspace to create a life that’s truly our own.

Because here’s the thing: you are so much more powerful than you realise. Your thoughts shape your reality. And when you shift your mindset, you shift your life. My mission isn’t just to help you feel better about being single—it’s to help you recognise your own agency. To help you see that you are the creator of your own experience. And that you, and you alone, get to decide what your life looks like.

So join me here every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday, and let’s build lives that feel joyful, meaningful, and wildly fulfilling — on our own terms.

Let’s Thrive Solo…together.

Coe Author with Robin Coe is a journey into stories, dreams, consciousness, and the strange spaces between what we call real and what we imagine. Each episode, Robin reads a chapter from her fiction, along with poetry, essays, and reflections on the ideas, experiences, and unexpected moments of synchronicity that inspire her writing.
Come for the stories. Stay for the questions they leave behind.

title: The NoCo Tag Team Advantage Podcast
author: The Sherman Team
description: Real estate, life advice, and Colorado stories from a mother–son tag team who’ve spent years helping people navigate homes, transitions, and the moments that shape everyday life. We break down the market, share behind‑the‑scenes experiences, talk through real challenges buyers and sellers face, and mix in family dynamics, local insight, and the humor that comes with working side‑by‑side in Northern Colorado.

description:

title: Love in Practice
author: Therapy with Isabella
description:
Love is more than something we feel. It’s something we practice.
Love in Practice is about what happens when love meets real life—the ways we reach for each other, protect ourselves, hurt each other, lose each other, and find our way back.
Hosted by couples therapist Isabella Alonzo-Gatti, LMFT, the show looks beneath our patterns to the stories underneath them: the families we came from, the histories we carry, and the larger, often invisible forces that shape how we love.
Love not as an ideal, but as something we learn, live, and practice.

description:
Mike Hansen, MD, a critical care physician and medical educator, works through clinical cases and explains his reasoning: what matters, how the evidence fits, and what each case can teach us.

title: The India AI Brief
author: Balaji Rao
description: AI is moving fast, and keeping up can feel like a full-time job. The India AI Brief explores the latest AI developments, interesting Indian startups, new tools and capabilities, and what it all means for people building businesses and working with AI. Short, thoughtful explainers for founders, builders, business owners and curious early adopters. Less hype, more context. Let's figure it out together.

title: Still Unanswered
author: Theresa Michaels & David Zarza
description:
For each case, David is given only the subject's name, date of birth and photograph. Theresa researches the case independently. When they come together, David has no knowledge of what Theresa has uncovered. Together they examine what connects, what doesn't, and what may still be waiting to be uncovered.


Theresa and David first met more than a decade ago when David appeared on Theresa's television series, Twisted & Listed. Their backgrounds couldn't be more different, but what began as an unexpected meeting became a lasting friendship. Despite their very different perspectives, they share a genuine desire to help the people and families they work with.

Still Unanswered grew from that friendship.


Theresa Michaels has spent more than three decades in real estate and pioneered the real-estate niche now known as crime and stigmatized properties - homes connected to tragedy and circumstances far outside the ordinary. Her work has taken her beyond the properties themselves, into the stories of the people and events connected to them.

David Zarza is a Seattle-based psychic medium and intuitive life coach, as well as a published author. For decades, his work has been rooted in intuition, connection and insight, helping individuals and families navigate questions, transitions and circumstances in their lives.

title: Holistic Hitting The Podcast
author: Holistic Hitting
description:
Welcome to the Holistic Hitting Podcast, hosted by former Major League player and hitting coach Andy Barkett.
This podcast is dedicated to helping hitters, coaches, and parents better understand what it really takes to develop elite hitters and championship-level competitors.
Drawing on over two decades of experience in professional baseball—as a Major League player, Major League hitting coach, minor league coordinator, and private instructor—Andy breaks down the mechanics, movements, routines, and mental skills that separate great hitters from the rest.

title: Mark Larson Unfiltered
author: Mark Larson
description:
Mark Larson Unfiltered is the independent San Diego news and commentary podcast from longtime radio host Mark Larson, who has been on San Diego airwaves for 50 years.
Free from the format clock and commercial breaks, Mark takes on San Diego news and politics, City Hall, local issues, and the national stories everyone is talking about. Expect honest opinions, local perspective, and stories from half a century in broadcasting.
New episodes weekly. Subscribe so you don't miss one, and tell a friend.

title: Inside The High Performance Edge
author: Nick Poulos
description: Great performances begin long before game day. Inside The High Performance Edge with Dr Nick Poulos explores the people, systems, and decisions behind success in sport and business. In conversation with Lee Woodward and expert guests, Nick draws on 25+ years in international elite sport to share practical lessons on building teams, aligning people, and leading under pressure. One focused topic at a time, discover insights you can apply to your own team, business, and leadership. Understand your people, align your team, prepare to perform.
